source.title: Hallucination Neurons and Where to Find Them: An Investigation into the existence of Hallucination Neurons
source.authors: Huseyin Cavus; Sebin Sabu; J. Spear; J. Kawatra; Pavithra Rajendran

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates whether sparse neuron selections in LLMs are uniquely localized. Its diagnostics indicate that selected neurons often have correlated alternatives and that selections vary across fitting procedures, refining how sparse-neuron evidence should be interpreted. It does not test toy-model superposition directly.
record.gate_note: Detection AUROCs and causal intervention effects concern hallucination detection and control, not the feature geometry or representation claims in the listed versions, so they are not rows. The paper mentions feature superposition as related context but does not test it. Rows below record the activation-correlation and selection-diagnostic results as indirect evidence relevant to V4.
record.test_reason: The study checks whether L1 sparse probes pick unique hallucination neurons in Gemma 3 4B / MedGemma 4B. It measures inter-neuron activation correlation, bootstrap stability of probe selections, and L1/L2 ranking overlap. These are collinearity diagnostics of a probing method. They do not measure whether features are spread across neurons in superposition, whether an SAE recovers sparse features, or any toy-model geometry. Superposition appears once in the Discussion (Sec 5.1), as context the results are 'consistent with'. Correlated neuron clusters have many possible causes, so they do not bear on V4 as named.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that sparse probing finds predictive neuron sets with significant population-level causal effects, but not uniquely localized ones. The selections sit in correlated clusters, are moderately stable under bootstrap, disagree between L1 and L2 rankings, and are only partly shared across datasets and models.
record.recipe_differences: This study adapts the H-Neurons identification pipeline and adds correlation, bootstrap, ranking, intervention-control, and overlap diagnostics; it does not reproduce the Toy Models of Superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset affected bootstrap stability and neuron-selection overlap; the study reports stronger stability for BioASQ than for TriviaQA and NQ-Open.

fits_no_version.finding: In Gemma 3 4B, 19/22 L1-selected hallucination-probe neurons have |r|>0.7 with non-selected neurons. Bootstrap selection Jaccard is 0.45–0.69 and L1/L2 top-k overlap is 0–25%. The hallucination signal is carried by correlated neuron clusters, not unique units.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Behaviour-predictive signals in LLM MLP activations are spread over correlated neuron clusters, so sparse-probe neuron selections are non-unique and unstable.

record.problems: Only two checkpoints, both in the Gemma 3 4B family, were evaluated. The representation evidence is indirect: neuron activation correlations and probe-selection diagnostics do not directly establish feature decomposition or feature dimensionality. The authors did not test capability preservation after intervention.
record.rows_left_out: Detection and causal-intervention results were not included because they measure hallucination detection/control rather than the listed representation versions. Cross-dataset and cross-model neuron-set overlaps were also omitted because they measure recurrence of selected indices across settings, not whether features are distributed across neurons.

untested.parts: All: no toy networks, sparsity sweeps or feature geometry.
All: no test of capacity pressure or feature importance.
All: no measure of how features spread across neurons and no SAE. Neuron correlation clusters from probing are not that measure.
All: no SAE features are studied.
All: feature dimensionality is not examined.

missing.what: NQ-Open bootstrap Jaccard 0.45 (D2) has no row, although the TriviaQA and BioASQ D2 values do.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T5' on V4 and its supports/limits_scope labels are removed. The paper is a methodological critique of H-Neuron sparse probing and cites Toy Models of Superposition only as background. Even read generously, inter-neuron correlation does not show features superposed across neurons. All diagnostics come from one 4B model family, and the authors call their thresholds empirical guidelines.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks, feature sparsity, overlap geometry, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry.
Whether capacity pressure causes polysemanticity or how feature importance affects dedicated versus shared dimensions.
Whether polysemantic neurons arise without capacity pressure.
The study provides indirect evidence about correlated alternatives to sparse neuron selections, but does not directly decompose features across neurons or test whether an SAE recovers them.
Whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
Whether represented features are one-dimensional directions or multidimensional.

rows.subject: Gemma 3 4B
rows.operation_detail: Measured the fraction of selected H-Neurons with a non-selected feature having Pearson |r| > 0.7.
rows.measure: Selected H-Neurons correlated above the threshold with another feature
rows.baseline: Localization concern threshold: more than approximately 30% of neurons with a high-correlation partner
rows.note: The authors interpret the correlation as evidence that L1 selects from correlated clusters; this is indirect evidence about distributed representation, not a direct feature decomposition.
rows.check: Measures neuron–neuron activation correlation for L1-selected probe features, a probe-collinearity diagnostic, not features distributed across neurons. 'partial' was unjustified: 70% exceeds the authors' 30% concern threshold. The TriviaQA diagnostics come from an independent replicate with 10 H-Neurons, not the Table 1 run with 9.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Gemma 3 4B on TriviaQA, BioASQ, and NQ-Open
reader_labels.reason: Selected neurons had correlated non-selected alternatives and sparse-versus-dense rankings disagreed, supporting indirect evidence of correlated representation structure rather than unique neuron localization (r1-r3, r6-r8).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Bootstrap stability across the three Gemma 3 4B dataset settings
reader_labels.reason: Selection stability was moderate and below the study's suggested 0.7 threshold, so the indirect evidence does not establish a stable or canonical set of distributed features (r4-r5).
